cells.tense: The work is deepening right now, and both hands are on it.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Take one edge inside the work, where good stops and nearly good starts, and stay on that edge for a single session this week. Then set it down.
cells.core:
You're building, and the building is going well. The repetitions aren't grinding you down because something in them keeps getting truer, and bearing the weight doesn't feel like bracing. Time alone with the work connects you more than it cuts you off; you come back from it more yourself, not less. That's the shape of this when it holds, and it's holding.

What keeps it there is small on purpose. Take one edge inside the work, where good stops and nearly good starts, and stay on that edge for a single session this week. Then set it down. Going close on one line is how the whole thing stays alive — not a fix, just the line traced again, and the work stays yours while you do it.
cells.sheetLine: The building is going well and the hands are steady.
cells.verb: Deepening a craft through long, patient building
cells.place: Where you bear weight without going rigid

cells.tense: Tomorrow's version of the work is being lived in before it is made.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, the day it happens
cells.ask: When a piece of the work goes right, tell someone about it that same day. Not later, not once the whole thing is done.
cells.core:
You're braced for the version of this that isn't built yet. The finished thing is already in your head, so what your hands can do today reads as behind, and bearing the weight turns into pushing — gripping the work tighter than it needs. The strain is real, and it's mostly aimed at a day that hasn't arrived.

When a piece of the work goes right, tell someone about it that same day. Not later, not once the whole thing is done. Saying it out loud moves what you're measuring against — this hour instead of the far end — and eases the grip. Gladness is allowed to arrive early, ahead of the finished thing.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping a day that hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: Deepening a craft through long, patient building
cells.place: Where you bear weight without going rigid

cells.tense: The shape of what you built was never spoken out loud, and it still isn't.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Write down, in plain words, how you want one part of the work arranged. Put it where someone else could read it, and leave it there without explaining it.
cells.core:
The building has gone quiet. You still show up and the hands still know the way, but the arrangement you made lives in your head and nowhere else. So it can't carry any weight, and you carry all of it. Bearing that alone turns into waiting at a door you've already walked through.

Write down, in plain words, how you want one part of the work arranged. Put it where someone else could read it, and leave it there without explaining it. Saying the shape out loud is what lets it do some of the bearing. That half of this has been sitting unused, and it doesn't need a defense — just the frame on the table.
cells.sheetLine: You carry the shape of it alone, unsaid.

cells.tense: The steady building is running, and it has your name off it.
cells.act: find the rhythm and stay in it
cells.ask: Notice the pace you keep in the work, and change nothing about it for a week — only note, when you feel it, that you are the one holding it.
cells.core:
There's a steady rhythm in how you build — a pace you return to without deciding to, work that goes out at the speed you can actually hold. Asked about it, you'd say it's how the job goes. But every week someone selects that pace and stays with it, and that someone is you. What's yours is filed under circumstance.

Notice the pace you keep in the work, and change nothing about it for a week — only note, when you feel it, that you are the one holding it. The rhythm doesn't need improving. It needs an author standing beside it, and no more than that.
cells.sheetLine: The steady pace is your doing, filed under how the job goes.
cells.verb: Deepening a craft through long, patient building
cells.place: Where you bear weight without going rigid
